body:
🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 5)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: data  •  alerts in group: 1

*Headline:* `oauth_token` Mongo DB is **6000.81 GB (~6 TB)** — 1199× the bot's 5 GB advisory threshold. Backup completed OK, but the size warning is real.

*Bonus finding — B05PN7JG87L bot identity hypothesis (worth your eyes):* The bot whose 26+ block-only fires we've been treating as "opaque mystery noise" for 4+ weeks is **almost certainly the MongoDB Backup Status bot**. Today's fire is the first one whose text rendered in the plain message body (vs Slack blocks only), because it included a warning attachment. All historical B05PN7JG87L fires land at clean :35Z-ish minute boundaries consistent with overnight backup cron windows. If confirmed, ~26 prior "needs-human / low-impact" log entries are actually routine backup-completion noise.

Symptoms / signals:
  - Single Slack message: `:white_check_mark: MongoDB Backup Completed with Warning — Backup for database `oauth_token` completed. ⚠️ This database is 6000.81 GB, which exceeds 5GB and may impact future backup performance.`
  - No DD monitors firing on mongo/oauth
  - 0 thread replies (no operator engagement yet)
  - No oauth2 / ms-authentication-api deploys since 2026-05-25 — not deploy-correlated
  - DD log search for `oauth_token` / `MongoDB Backup` 09:00–11:10Z returned 0 hits (backup tool likely posts to Slack only)

Likely cause: `oauth_token` is the OAuth2/IdentityServer4 token store. 6 TB strongly suggests **expired/revoked tokens are not being cleaned up** — IdentityServer4's PersistedGrant cleanup job is probably not running (or never wired up). Not a current outage; will become operationally painful before it breaks.

Suggested next actions:
  1. Confirm/deny the B05PN7JG87L = MongoDB Backup Status bot hypothesis (would unblock ~26 retroactive re-classifications).
  2. Find the cleanup job for `oauth_token` in ms-authentication-api / oauth2 (IdentityServer4 `TokenCleanup` background service or equivalent). Verify it's enabled and running.
  3. File a defect / op ticket for the bloat — backup duration + restore time scale with DB size.
  4. Tighten `ki-mongodb-rs01-fd-exhaustion` KB match block: it currently has `{"contains": "MongoDB"}` and `{"contains": "mongod"}` which falsely matched this benign backup-completion message. Should require something specific like `fatal assertion 50882` / `EMFILE` / `errno 24` / `LimitNOFILE`.

Score breakdown:
  • +3 metric_breach_magnitude (6000.81 GB vs 5 GB threshold = ratio 1199 → ≥2.0 bracket)
  • +2 truly_novel_no_prior_hash (no prior alert_hash in incident-log; first visible-text B05PN7JG87L)
  • 0 critical_path_service (oauth2 is critical-path, but service isn't down — backup OK)
  • 0 active_users_affected (no user impact)
  • 0 deploy_correlation, 0 cross_channel_co_fire, 0 group_size_1, 0 account_tier
  • 0 matched_kb (the ki-mongodb-rs01-fd-exhaustion "match" is over-broad false-positive — treated as null)
  • 0 operator_engagement, 0 monitor_history (no monitor_id), 0 recency_decay

  • DD monitors: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/manage (none firing on mongo/oauth)
  • DD logs: https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=oauth_token%20OR%20%22MongoDB%20Backup%22&from_ts=1780218000000&to_ts=1780225680000&live=false
  • Investigation report: docs/investigations/2026-05-31-280112c3596d9bcc.md
  • Kibana: URL unavailable (KIBANA_BASE_URL unset in this run env)

Standing asks unchanged: (1) poll-cron still stuck since 2026-05-28T22:10Z (~60h dark, manual run #15); (2) ki-21 fix_status=needs-ops-decision 10+ days; (3) ki-24 fix_status=investigating occ 36 unchanged 8+ days; (4) **B05PN7JG87L identity hypothesis above is the lead we've been waiting for — please validate**.

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-21-gateway-microservices-timeout`
This is occurrence **#88** total (62nd group in the last 7 days).
**Playbook:** 1) Confirm chronic baseline by comparing ES `Ocelot.Responder.Middleware` warning volume in-window vs 24h ago (chronic if Δ < ±20%). 2) Aggregate timeouts by `RequestPath`; if upstream is `microservices.methodlocal.int` it's pool-level. 3) Check `ki-dns-microservices-method-int-pps-quota` first. 4) Identify which Tier-3 service owns the slow path via `ms-gateway-api/gateway/API/ocelot.*.json`. 5) Decision tree: (a) raise per-route Ocelot timeout (cheap, masks); (b) scale microservices IIS pool / shorten recycle; (c) profile upstream (sync-util / preferences / account).
